intro.title: useReducer vs useState
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple counter application twice—first using Vue's `ref` (similar to React's `useState`) and then using a custom `useReducer` function—to compare two state management approaches. You will learn the core concept of state management, focusing on when to use simple reactive state versus a reducer pattern for more complex logic. The main technologies involved are Vue 3's Composition API with `ref`, `computed`, and custom composable functions. By the end, you'll understand how `useReducer` centralizes state updates through actions, making your code more predictable and maintainable for certain use cases compared to `ref`.
intro.usecase: In real Vue applications, managing complex component state is crucial for features like multi-step forms, shopping carts, or dashboard controls. For example, an e-commerce checkout form with shipping options, payment methods, and promo codes requires coordinated state updates that useState alone can make messy. useReducer provides a cleaner solution for these scenarios by centralizing state logic, similar to how Vuex handles application-wide state but at the component level. This pattern appears in admin panels with filter systems, interactive data visualizations, and any UI where multiple actions affect the same state object.
